text: Import revamp, step 1 — a real pipeline: detect format by content not header line (skip preamble lines until a row with a date-like and money-like column; sniff ';' ',' tab over the first 20 lines; decode Windows-1252 when UTF-8 yields U+FFFD), and add readers for Santander .txt blocks, QIF and OFX/QFX (FITID) alongside CSV; offer the column mapper whenever detection is unsure instead of refusing.
evidence: js/core/moneyimport.js reads by content: OFX/QFX, QIF and Santander .txt readers (read(), :360-371; readOFX :291 with FITID, readQIF :313, readSantander :339), the CSV header row is found below a preamble by a date-and-amount row (:223-237), ';' ',' tab are sniffed (sniffDelimiter :147), Windows-1252 is used when bytes are not UTF-8 (decode :55), and the import dialog falls back to matching columns by hand (js/modules/moneyimp.js:6, mapping step :119-171).

text: Import revamp, step 2 — identity and reconciliation: store per row its source (bank, account, FITID or a hash of date+amount+description+balance+occurrence index) so the same statement re-imported is recognised whatever the mapping; use the Balance column to verify ordering and catch missing or duplicated rows ('Balance after 29 Oct should be £120.10, Money says £116.65'); match imported rows to confirmed recurring occurrences and typed entries (date ±3 days, same amount) and offer 'This is the same as …' instead of adding twins.
evidence: Built: each row stores an identity (bank id or a hash of its fields plus an occurrence count, idHash/imp, js/core/money.js:1144-1159, :1287-1312, normalised :645-649), re-imports are recognised (:1318-1366), the bank's Balance column is checked row by row (balanceCheck, js/core/moneyimport.js:420-438; shown at js/modules/moneyimp.js:253-258) and rows match recurring occurrences within 3 days (matchRules, money.js:1371-1412). Missing: typed (hand-entered) entries are only matched on the exact same day, amount and payee (legacy key, :1335-1347), with no '±3 days, This is the same as…' offer, and the bank balance is not compared with Money's own running total.
note: When a statement row looks like a payment you already typed in by hand a day or two apart, Money would ask 'Is this the same as…?' instead of adding it twice.

text: Import revamp, step 3 — information a Santander student needs: merchant normalisation ('HERON FOODS HOYLAND (VIA APPLE PAY), ON 29-10-2026' / 'CARD PAYMENT TO … RATE 1.00/GBP ON …' → 'Heron Foods', keeping the raw text as the note), Santander Type codes (DEB, DD, SO, FPI, FPO, BGC, CR, ATM) mapped to direction and kind, payee→category rules learned from the user's re-categorising ('Always put Heron Foods in Food'), recurring detection (same merchant, same amount, ~monthly → 'Make Google One a rule?'), spend by merchant and by week, and the account balance over time from the Balance column.

Missing: recurring detection only suggests Direct Debits and standing orders by their Type code (BANK_REPEATS, js/core/money.js:1431, :1475), not 'same merchant, same amount, about monthly' card payments such as Google One.
note: Money would also spot card payments that repeat every month for the same amount (like a Google One subscription) and offer to turn them into a recurring bill.

text: Routines inside routines: a step can reference another routine. Model: add step.sub = <routineId> in normaliseStep (js/core/routines.js:142). Display text and minutes are DERIVED from the sub-routine (mins = the sum of its required steps' mins), never copied. Integrity, enforced in normalise(rec, base) and in the editor: (a) no cycles: walk sub links depth-first from the routine being saved, refusing any step whose sub reaches the parent (also cap depth at 2, so a sub-routine cannot itself contain subs); (b) the sub-routine's total cannot exceed the parent step's budget. Either make the step's mins read-only (= sub total), or, if the user sets a budget, refuse a save of the sub that would push it over and say which parent step it breaks; (c) a sub-routine must be on demand or share the parent's days (kind/anchor), otherwise it would also show on its own schedule. Keep 'days: null' (on demand) as the rule for anything used as a sub; (d) deleting a routine used as a sub is refused, or offers to unlink (steps become plain text with the last derived minutes). Logging: ticking a sub step in the player expands the sub's steps inline, and the parent step counts done when the sub's own completion rule is met that routine day. The sub's log entry is written under its own key with a parent tag, so it pays nothing on its own (pay once per invariant 143: only the parent pays). snapOf must store the sub's id and its frozen step list in the parent's snapshot (x[6] = sub snapshot), so editing the sub never rewrites a past day. The cloud merge needs no change (steps merge whole with the routine). Player: a nested progress bar, 'Shower · from Morning hygiene (3 steps)'.
evidence: normaliseStep (js/core/routines.js:145-159) keeps only id, text, mins, optional, minimum, checkMorning, note, link and at; there is no step.sub or any routine-to-routine reference in routines.js.
note: A step in one routine could be a whole other routine (for example Morning runs your Skincare routine), with its steps shown inside, its time added up for you and paid only once.
